literal: West of the temple was Changtai County, and farther west Tianchang Abbey.
idiomatic: West of the temple lay Changtai County and, beyond it, Tianchang Abbey.

literal: Southwest was the Directorate of Education; north of it Confucius Temple; east of the temple Jieyi Temple.
idiomatic: Southwest stood the Directorate of Education; north of it the Confucius Temple; east of that Jieyi Temple.

literal: Farther northwest Anguo Temple, built by Taizong.
idiomatic: Farther northwest was Anguo Temple, Taizong's foundation.

literal: East of the temple was the former residence of Empress Qitian; east of that the Yuan Consort residence built by Empress Fatian.
idiomatic: East of the temple stood Empress Qitian's former residence; beyond it the Yuan Consort residence that Empress Fatian built.

literal: South were Jushengni Temple, the Brocade Office, Inner Secretariat, Qu Office, and the two granaries Zanguo and Shengsi—all southwest of the Great Inner; the Eight Crafts Office faced Tianxiong Temple.
idiomatic: To the south lay Jushengni Temple, the Brocade Office, Inner Secretariat, Qu Office, and the Zanguo and Shengsi granaries—all southwest of the Great Inner, with the Eight Crafts Office opposite Tianxiong Temple.

literal: The south city was called the Han City; facing the cross street south, each had a tower standing opposite, with market stalls below.
idiomatic: The southern quarter was the Han City; along the cross street paired gate-towers faced each other above rows of market stalls.

literal: North of the east gate was Lu County; southeast of that Xingren County.
idiomatic: North of the east gate stood Lu County; southeast of it Xingren County.

literal: East of the south gate was the Uighur Camp where Uighur merchants staying at Shangjing were quartered.
idiomatic: East of the south gate lay the Uighur Camp, housing merchants from Uighur lands who traded at Shangjing.

literal: Southwest Tongwen Hostel housed envoys from various states.
idiomatic: Southwest, Tongwen Hostel lodged envoys from foreign states.

literal: Southwest of the hostel was Linhuang Hostel, awaiting Xia envoys.
idiomatic: Southwest of that stood Linhuang Hostel for Xia envoys.

literal: West of the hostel Fuxian Temple.
idiomatic: West of the hostel was Fuxian Temple.

literal: West of the temple Xuanhua County; southwest Dingba County; west of the county Baohe County.
idiomatic: West of the temple lay Xuanhua County; southwest Dingba; west of that Baohe County.

literal: North of the west gate Yisu County; east of the county Qianliao County.
idiomatic: North of the west gate was Yisu County; east of it Qianliao County.

literal: In the Guangshun era of Later Zhou, Hu Qiao's Record says: at Shangjing's west tower were houses and market stalls; trade used cloth, not coin.
idiomatic: Hu Qiao's Record from Later Zhou's Guangshun era notes that Shangjing's west tower quarter had houses and markets where cloth served as currency.

literal: There were brocade workshops, eunuchs, Hanlin, artisans, music offices, wrestlers, Confucians, monks and nuns, and Daoists.
idiomatic: The city held brocade workshops, eunuchs, Hanlin academicians, artisans, music bureaus, wrestlers, Confucians, monks, nuns, and Daoists.

literal: Chinese were mostly from Bing, Fen, You, and Ji.
idiomatic: Han residents came chiefly from Bing, Fen, You, and Ji.

literal: In the ninth year of Song Dazhong Xiangfu, Xue Ying's Record says: from Zhongjing due north eighty li to Songshan Station, seventy li to Chongxin Station, ninety li to Guangning Station, fifty li to Yaojiazhai Station, fifty li to Xianning Station, thirty li crossing the Huang River stone bridge—beside it Rao Prefecture, where Tang once placed Rao Marsh Prefecture and Bohai now lived.
idiomatic: Xue Ying's Record of Song Dazhong Xiangfu year 9 describes the route north from Zhongjing: eighty li to Songshan Station, seventy to Chongxin, ninety to Guangning, fifty to Yaojiazhai, fifty to Xianning, then thirty li over the Huang River stone bridge by Rao Prefecture—Tang's old Rao Marsh seat, now home to Bohai settlers.

literal: Fifty li to Baohe Station, crossing Hei River, seventy li to Xuanhua Station, fifty li to Changtai Station.
idiomatic: Fifty li farther lay Baohe Station; crossing the Hei River, seventy li to Xuanhua Station and fifty to Changtai Station.

literal: Twenty li west of the station was a Buddhist shrine and dwellings—these were Zu Prefecture.
idiomatic: Twenty li west of the station stood a shrine and houses marking Zu Prefecture.

literal: Another forty li to Linhuang Prefecture; after passing Chongxin Station one entered old Khitan territory—south of it was Xi land.
idiomatic: Forty li more reached Linhuang Prefecture; beyond Chongxin Station lay the old Khitan heartland, with Xi territory to the south.

literal: Entering the west gate, the gate called Jinde; within was Linhuang Hostel; the inner east gate called Shunyang.
idiomatic: The west gate Jinde led to Linhuang Hostel inside; the inner east gate was Shunyang.

literal: Going north to Jingfu Gate, then to Chengtian Gate; within were Zhaode and Xuanzheng halls; with felt tents all faced east.
idiomatic: Northward lay Jingfu Gate, then Chengtian Gate; inside stood Zhaode and Xuanzheng halls, all facing east like the felt tents.

literal: Northwest of Linhuang more than two hundred li was called Liangdian, south of Mantou Mountain—a place to escape summer heat.
idiomatic: More than two hundred li northwest of Linhuang lay Liangdian south of Mantou Mountain, a summer retreat.

literal: Grass was abundant; digging a zhang or more down brought hard ice.
idiomatic: Pasture was rich; a zhang below ground one struck hard ice.

literal: Zu Prefecture, Tiancheng Army, upper grade, military commission.
idiomatic: Zu Prefecture—Tiancheng Army, upper grade, with a military commissioner.

literal: Originally the hereditary lands of the Liao Right Eight Divisions.
idiomatic: It had been the hereditary domain of the Liao Right Eight Divisions.

literal: Taizu often autumn-hunted here and first set up Xilou.
idiomatic: Taizu hunted here each autumn and first established Xilou.

literal: Later a city was built and called Zu Prefecture.
idiomatic: A city followed, named Zu Prefecture.

literal: Because it was the birthplace of the High Ancestor Zhaolie Emperor, the Great-Grandfather Zhuangjing Emperor, the Grandfather Jianxian Emperor, and the Imperial Father Xuanjian Emperor, it took this name.
idiomatic: It commemorated the birthplaces of the High Ancestor Zhaolie, Great-Grandfather Zhuangjing, Grandfather Jianxian, and Imperial Father Xuanjian emperors.

literal: The wall was two zhang high, without fighting galleries; the circuit nine li.
idiomatic: Walls stood two zhang high without fighting galleries; the circuit ran nine li.

literal: Gates: east Wangjing, south Daxia, west Yeshan, north Xingguo.
idiomatic: Gates were Wangjing east, Daxia south, Yeshan west, and Xingguo north.

literal: In the northwest corner was an inner city.
idiomatic: A northwest inner city lay within the walls.

literal: Halls called Liangming, enshrining ancestral portraits;
idiomatic: The Liangming Hall enshrined ancestral portraits;

literal: called Eryi, casting Taizu's image in white gold;
idiomatic: the Eryi Hall held a white-gold image of Taizu;

literal: called Heilong and Qingmi, each keeping Taizu's early weapons, utensils, and fur garments to show posterity and not forget origins.
idiomatic: Heilong and Qingmi halls preserved Taizu's early weapons, gear, and furs so posterity would not forget their roots.

literal: The inner south gate was Xingsheng; three gates in all had tower-pavilions; east and west had corner towers.
idiomatic: The inner south gate Xingsheng headed three gated towers; corner towers stood east and west.

literal: East were the prefectural offices and various palace offices; the Brocade Office shift and attendants—Fan, Han, and Bohai three hundred persons—supplied the inner palace on demand.
idiomatic: East lay prefectural offices and palace bureaus; brocade shifts and attendants—three hundred Fan, Han, and Bohai staff—met inner-palace requisitions.

literal: On the southeast cross street the four corners had facing towers linked to market stalls below.
idiomatic: Along the southeast cross street corner towers faced one another above linked market rows.

literal: East Changba County, west Xianning County.
idiomatic: East stood Changba County; west, Xianning County.

literal: There was Zu Mountain with Taizu's Heavenly Emperor Temple; his riding boots still remained.
idiomatic: Zu Mountain held Taizu's Heavenly Emperor Temple, where his riding boots were still kept.

literal: There were also Longmen, Ligu, Yeshan, Yequan, Baima, Dushi, and Tianti mountains.
idiomatic: Landmarks included Longmen, Ligu, Yeshan, Yequan, Baima, Dushi, and Tianti peaks.

literal: Waters were the south Sha River and west Yequan.
idiomatic: Waters included the south Sha River and west Yequan.

literal: Taizu's tomb carved the mountain into a hall called Ming Hall.
idiomatic: Taizu's tomb hollowed the mountain into the Ming Hall.

literal: South of the hall on the ridge was a feast hall for seasonal sacrifices.
idiomatic: A feast hall on the southern ridge served seasonal rites.

literal: The gate was called Heilong.
idiomatic: Its gate was named Heilong.

literal: To the east was Shengji Hall with a stele describing Taizu's hunting.
idiomatic: East lay Shengji Hall, whose stele recorded Taizu's hunts.

literal: East of the hall was a tower with a stele commemorating Taizu's founding achievement.
idiomatic: East of the hall a tower bore a stele on Taizu's founding deeds.

literal: All were five li west of the prefecture.
idiomatic: All lay five li west of the prefectural seat.

literal: Built in the Tianxian era by Taizong; subordinate to Hongyi Palace.
idiomatic: Taizong built it in the Tianxian era; it belonged to Hongyi Palace.

literal: It ruled two counties and one walled town: Changba County.
idiomatic: It governed two counties and one walled town—Changba County.

literal: Originally people of Longzhou's Changping County, moved here.
idiomatic: Settlers came from Longzhou's Changping County.

literal: Households 2,000.
idiomatic: 2,000 households.

literal: Xianning County.
idiomatic: County seat: Xianning.

literal: Originally Changning County.
idiomatic: It had been Changning County.

literal: When Liaoyang was taken its people were moved and settled.
idiomatic: After Liaoyang fell its people were resettled here.

literal: Households 1,000.
idiomatic: 1,000 households.

literal: Prince of Yue walled town.
idiomatic: Prince of Yue Fortified Town.

literal: Taizu's paternal uncle, campaigning west against Tangut and Tuhun, herded captives here and therefore built a city.
idiomatic: Taizu's paternal uncle, campaigning west against Tangut and Tuhun, pastured captives here and walled a town.

literal: It lay twenty li southeast of the prefecture.
idiomatic: It stood twenty li southeast of the prefecture.

literal: Households 1,000.
idiomatic: 1,000 households.

literal: Fuyu County.
idiomatic: Fuyu County.

literal: Originally Longquan Prefecture.
idiomatic: It had been Longquan Prefecture.

literal: Taizu moved surrendered Bohai Fuyu County households here; Shizong established the county.
idiomatic: Taizu resettled surrendered Bohai households from Fuyu County; Shizong created the county.

literal: Households 1,500.
idiomatic: 1,500 households.

literal: Xianli County.
idiomatic: Xianli County.

literal: Originally people of Xianli Prefecture; Taizu attacked Bohai, captured King Da Yinzhen, and moved the people here; Shizong established the county.
idiomatic: Originally Xianli Prefecture people; when Taizu conquered Bohai and seized King Da Yinzhen he resettled them here; Shizong founded the county.

literal: Households 1,000.
idiomatic: 1,000 households.

literal: Qing Prefecture, Xuanning Army, upper grade, military commission.
idiomatic: Qing Prefecture—Xuanning Army, upper grade, with a military commissioner.

literal: Originally the land of Taibao Mountain and Hei River; valleys and passes were steep and narrow.
idiomatic: Its soil was Taibao Mountain and the Hei River country—rugged valleys and narrow passes.

literal: Muzong built a city called Hei River Prefecture; each year he came to hunt tigers and hawk eagles, and most military affairs were entrusted to great ministers.
idiomatic: Muzong walled Hei River Prefecture, visited yearly to hunt tigers and hawks, and left most military affairs to senior ministers.

literal: Later he was assassinated here.
idiomatic: He was later assassinated on this ground.

literal: Because the land was bitter cold, in the eighth year of Tonghe the prefecture was abolished.
idiomatic: The bitter cold led Tonghe year 8 to abolish the prefecture.

literal: Shengzong autumn-hunted, loved its strange beauty, and established the name Qing Prefecture.
idiomatic: Shengzong hunted here in autumn, admired its rugged beauty, and revived it as Qing Prefecture.

literal: Liao's fifth-generation ancestor Botu had an unusual appearance, martial stratagem, strength to match a hundred men, and the masses pushed him as king.
idiomatic: Liao's fifth-generation ancestor Botu looked unlike others, possessed martial cunning, strength to match a hundred men, and was acclaimed king.

literal: Born on Botu Mountain, it took the name; when he died he was buried below the mountain.
idiomatic: He was born on Botu Mountain, which gave its name; at death he was buried beneath it.

literal: It was two hundred li from the prefecture.
idiomatic: The mountain lay two hundred li from the prefectural seat.

literal: Qingyun Mountain was originally Heiling.
idiomatic: Qingyun Mountain had formerly been Heiling.

literal: Shengzong halted and admired it, saying: "After my ten thousand years I shall be buried here."
idiomatic: Shengzong paused there and said, "When my ten thousand years are fulfilled, bury me here."

literal: Xingzong followed the testament and built Yongqing Tomb.
idiomatic: Xingzong obeyed the command and built Yongqing Tomb.

literal: There were Wangxian Hall and imperial portrait hall.
idiomatic: It held Wangxian Hall and a hall for imperial portraits.

literal: Three thousand Fan and Han tomb-guard households were set, all subordinate to the Great Inner Chief Steward Office.
idiomatic: Three thousand Fan and Han tomb-guard households were assigned under the Great Inner chief steward.

literal: Twenty li west of the prefecture.
idiomatic: It lay twenty li west of the prefectural seat.

literal: There were Hei Mountain, Chi Mountain, Taibao Mountain, Laoweng Ridge, Mantou Mountain, Xingguo Lake, Xiaoshi Marsh, and Hei River.
idiomatic: Features included Hei, Chi, and Taibao mountains, Laoweng Ridge, Mantou Mountain, Xingguo Lake, Xiaoshi Marsh, and the Hei River.

literal: Restored in the first year of Jingfu; later subordinate to Xingsheng Palace.
idiomatic: Restored in Jingfu year 1 and later attached to Xingsheng Palace.

literal: It ruled three counties:
idiomatic: It governed three counties:

literal: Xuande County.
idiomatic: Xuande County.

literal: Originally Hei Mountain and Hei River land.
idiomatic: Originally the Hei Mountain and Hei River region.

literal: In the first year of Jingfu, scattered-account households were gathered and settled as convenient.
idiomatic: Jingfu year 1 gathered scattered-account households for settlement where convenient.

literal: Households 6,000.
idiomatic: 6,000 households.

literal: Xiao'an County.
idiomatic: Xiao'an County.

literal: Fuyi County.
idiomatic: Fuyi County.

literal: Originally Yi Prefecture; Taizong moved Bohai Yi Prefecture people here.
idiomatic: Originally Yi Prefecture; Taizong resettled Bohai people from Yi Prefecture here.

literal: In the first year of Chongxi it was demoted to Yifeng County, later renamed.
idiomatic: Chongxi year 1 demoted it to Yifeng County, later renamed Fuyi.

literal: Subordinate to Hongyi Palace.
idiomatic: It belonged to Hongyi Palace.

literal: Tai Prefecture, Dechang Army, military commission.
idiomatic: Tai Prefecture—Dechang Army with a military commissioner.

literal: Originally pasture land of the Khitan twenty tribal divisions.
idiomatic: Originally grazing land of the Khitan twenty divisions.

literal: Because the Black-Rat tribe repeatedly raided Tonghua Prefecture and the people could not resist, they moved six hundred li southeast, built a city, and dwelt near their own tribe.
idiomatic: When the Black-Rat tribe repeatedly struck Tonghua and locals could not repel them, the court shifted six hundred li southeast, walled a city, and settled near the parent tribe.

literal: Black-Rats dwelt in burrows, skin black, snouts sharp, resembling rats—hence the name.
idiomatic: The Black-Rats lived in burrows with black skin and sharp snouts like rats—hence the name.

literal: The prefecture was subordinate to Yanqing Palace; military affairs belonged to the Northeast Commandery Army Office.
idiomatic: The prefecture fell under Yanqing Palace; military affairs came under the Northeast Commandery Army Office.

literal: It ruled two counties:
idiomatic: It governed two counties:
